correctness.rationale: A pair of differently coloured adjacent true twins would each demand strictly more neighbours of its own colour than the other twin colour; identical external neighbourhoods make these demands contradictory. This forces every clique fibre monochromatic. Exact neighbour counts are \(s-1+s t_{c(v)}\) for the local colour and \(s t_d\) for another; for integer counts and \(s\ge2\), strict comparison is exactly \(t_{c(v)}\ge t_d\), valid for all base degrees and palettes. On path/cycle bases, this is equivalent to the absence of singleton runs. The path stars-and-bars factor and circular \(n/r\) boundary-marking factor count all runs without duplication; proper colourings of cyclic run adjacency are counted by the stated cycle chromatic factor, with \(r=2\) checked separately. Degree and leading coefficients follow. The packaged verifier independently examines actual open neighbourhoods for 34 finite cases and 1,969,502 assignments, and all counts agree. Finite checks do not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating Jones–Winkeler theorem proves existence of a polynomial and a general partition expansion; its examined specific clique-network examples are not complete inter-fibre joins, and no explicit binomial path/cycle-clique family theorem was found. The distinct earlier locally-optimal circular-ladder counting result concerns a Cartesian cycle–edge graph of degree three, not the lexicographic clique blowup (degree \(3s-1\), at least five); it neither implies the true-twin weak-plurality bijection nor the run formula. Targeted literature and semantic database queries did not uncover equivalent or stronger coverage. The reduction, clique-size invariance, and both closed evaluations are the claimed novel scope; priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: The recent strict-gridlock polynomial is motivated by exact counts of stable non-consensus states and its known general recurrence can grow exponentially. This theorem supplies a closed evaluation for every path/cycle clique blowup, including all maximum-degree-two base unions, and resolves the entire dependence on clique size by proving there is none when \(s\ge2\). The result computes exact named-colour counts, polynomial degree, leading coefficient and strict gridlock, for graph degrees unbounded with \(s\), giving natural community-network comparisons rather than arbitrary finite cases. It is more than a fixed instance or a generic restatement of the pre-existing partition expansion.
